en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Cittalatā Grove, from the Itthivimāna (The Mansion of Women) Section.
2. The Story of the Lakhumā Deva’s Mansion “O goddess,
with such exquisite beauty with which you stand there— ”
Illuminating all directions like a star among the herbs,
by what means do you possess such a complexion?
By what means do you succeed here?
For all those riches that are dear to the mind arise for you.
I ask you, O goddess of great majesty:
what merit did you perform while being a human?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing power?
"And your radiance illuminates all directions.
Thus questioned by Moggallāna, that deity was uplifted in mind.
When asked the question, she explained it—
the fruit of which deed this is:
"Having gone out through the gateway of the fishermen..."
My dwelling was there;
and as the disciples of the Great Seer were walking about therein, [I saw them].
I gave boiled rice, gruel, vegetables, and sour salted porridge to those who had become upright.
With a serene mind,
on the fourteenth, the fifteenth,
and the eighth day of the fortnight.
And during the fortnight of miracles,
I shall observe the Uposatha day, perfectly endowed with its eight factors.
Always restrained in our virtue,
self-controlled and generous,
we dwell here in this celestial mansion.
Abstaining from taking life,
restrained from false speech,
and from theft and sexual misconduct,
And far removed from the drinking of intoxicants,
they delight in the five precepts and are skilled in the Noble Truths.
I am a female lay follower of Gotama, the illustrious one who possesses the eye;
by that [merit], my complexion is such as this.
"...and so on... my complexion shines forth in all directions.
And, venerable sir, you should pay homage with your head at the Blessed One’s feet in my name, saying: [and so on]... "my complexion shines forth in all directions."
“Venerable sir, the female lay follower named Lakhumā pays homage with her head at the Blessed One’s feet.
“It is not surprising, venerable sir, that the Blessed One should have declared me [to be established] in one of the fruits of recluseship;
rather, it is the Blessed One who has declared me [to be established] in the fruit of a once-returner.”
The second is the Lakhumā vimāna.
